invariants: Original default maximum parallel-safe tool calls is ten, not eight. Deployment configuration and direct service construction refuse non-positive/non-integer/non-number values; whole numeric floats are admitted as original Number integers.

The optional agent-loop settings section contains only maxParallelToolCalls. Stored updates override composition, invalid writes retain the prior cap, provider detachment falls back to composition and consumer unloading releases the namespace.
The factory model loop actually passes the current cap to the scheduler; controlled twelve-call consumers at caps one/two/ten retain model-order result identities and perform the next model request.
The cap is read at each scheduler group boundary; changing settings cannot alter a group already in flight. A separate controlled group-snapshot observation is required before integration.

Fresh actual Source/native and isolated extracted observations must retain complete ordered identities and all imported candidate runtime module hashes. Omitted/reordered/changed rows, absent modules, foreign roots/Python or stale Source receipts refuse.

The complete clean candidate must pass all pytest, eighteen unchanged Source groups including the original 27 scheduler/settings assertions, all selected paired drivers and actual extracted/original-browser acceptance. Existing failures and scoped bug predicates are retained without retries or new exceptions.
identity: Pinned original group scheduler/configuration/settings, actual tool call IDs and candidate-imported module bytes identify these bounded observations.
ownership: The loop composition owns the base cap and configured agents; optional settings owns stored overrides; reversible injection releases namespace bindings and keeps composed agents out of editable settings.
ordering: Read one cap when starting a group, retain it while draining that group, read again after an exclusive barrier; commit results and next-request history in model order.
errors: Bounded direct numeric/configuration refusal and invalid settings writes; arbitrary public extension/error ABI and combined Tools/Wire remain separate.
cancellation: The existing scheduler abort/first-failure drain behavior is unchanged; this contract does not certify every simultaneous approval/followup/cancel/disposal combination.
adaptation: Python3.8 uses finite integer-number validation, owned asyncio pools and the canonical optional SettingsProvider; no product Node or original frontend changes.
open_questions: Full B2 combinations and arbitrary synchronous dispatch prefixes, complete UI/profile journeys and overall migration remain unaccepted.
Historical ReplaceFileW1175, startup cancellation, unmeasured partial-wire timeout, fixed-wait Source cache failure and Proactor warning remain independently unrooted; real Win7 stays deferred.
